works.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of renewable energy integration requires large-format lithium iron phosphate batteries with higher capacity and extended lifetime, which also introduces new safety and monitoring challenges. Internal temperature is a key determinant of battery performance, degradation, and safety, yet conventional methods such as embedded thermocouples or thermal simulations are impractical for large cells. Here, we present a non-invasive strategy using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy to reconstruct internal temperature. By integrating equivalent circuit model and distribution of relaxation times with mutual information-based frequency selection, we establish reliable impedance–temperature correlations. Furthermore, a physics-informed neural network embedding Arrhenius constraints improves accuracy, reducing prediction error to 1.092 °C. The method is validated not only at the single-cell level but also scaled to a 30-cell module while maintaining high precision. This impedance-based thermal mapping provides a scalable, accurate, and non-destructive tool for monitoring large-capacity lithium iron phosphate batteries, with potential to enhance the safety, reliability, and intelligent thermal management of grid-scale energy storage systems.
